A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 12-concept benchmark study despite changes to the title and benchmark name. Text, figures, and tables are readable throughout, including v3 Appendices A–F; v1 contains no appendix. Internal reporting inconsistencies limit some exact comparisons but do not prevent reliable assessment of the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original model and human evaluations in Figures 4–5, prompting experiments in Table 2, and a GPT-4o conservation/counting case study in Figure 6.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark evaluations, correlation and scaling analyses, and Concept Hacking results comparing models and humans, with additional analyses in Appendices D–F.

M1.justification: v3 introduces Concept Hacking, a systematic diagnostic procedure that reverses ground truth through task-relevant manipulations while preserving irrelevant conditions (Section 5.1). This substantially extends v1’s isolated conservation/counting example into paired tests distinguishing conceptual understanding, shortcuts, and illusory understanding. The benchmark renaming and retained ten prompting techniques do not themselves change the method.

E1.justification: The original 12 concepts remain, but v3 adds 45 paired standard/manipulated Concept Hacking scenarios and data analyses covering 26 other benchmarks and nine SEED-Bench abilities. These substantially extend evaluation conditions and analytical coverage. Appendix B’s omitted video-image-text row does not establish removal of that format, which remains illustrated in Figure 9.

E2.justification: The model comparison expands from approximately 46 models in v1, whose counts vary between passages, to 231 tested and 219 retained in v3. Table 2 verifies additional comparators including Qwen2.5-VL, NVLM-D, and LLaVA-Video models absent from v1 Figure 5. Appendix D.2 also adds comparisons of Exact, In, Template, and LLM matching against the hybrid matcher.

E3.justification: Circular zero-shot evaluation is retained, while v3 adds chance-normalized log accuracy, modality-dependent evaluation subsets, paired manipulation controls, and a reported 20% matching-failure exclusion threshold. Reported question screening changes from 95% reviewer correctness to over 80% across 20 human answers. Appendix B lists 2,299 questions, conflicting with v3’s main-text total of 2,519, so the exact revised sample remains unresolved.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained prompting study, v3 adds within-benchmark and cross-benchmark correlation analyses, parameter-scaling analyses, systematic Concept Hacking tests, and output-matching diagnostics. Appendix E examines GPT-4o’s explanations across manipulated examples. These substantially broaden the investigation of dependencies, scalability, evaluation failures, and shortcut reliance beyond v1’s single conservation/counting case.

E5.justification: v3 supplements v1’s point accuracies with distributions across models/prompts and scaling-fit error bars or bands, alongside regression R-squared values (Figures 3, 6, and 13). The uncertainty conventions are not adequately defined. Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, or formal significance tests; expanded model and prompt coverage does not establish additional repeated runs.

E6.justification: v3 adds model scores and extensive correlation, scaling, and manipulation results. New empty-prompt scaling fits report R-squared values of 0.304 for mechanical reasoning and 0.015 for perspective-taking (Figure 6). The prompting finding changes from most prompts helping in v1 Section 4 to most not improving performance in v3 Appendix F. Changed model pools and settings limit direct performance comparisons.

T1.justification: Appendix D.2 introduces an explicit mathematical definition of matching fail_rate, absent from v1. Its numerator counts valid matches, contradicting its interpretation as a failure rate. This is a limited formal addition; the expanded cognitive-science framework remains conceptual, with no new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The reversed-development observation is retained, but v3 adds central claims about missing human-like dependencies between abilities, weak scaling of low-level cognition, and shortcut-taking or illusory understanding instead of acquired core knowledge. Concept Hacking becomes a principal contribution in the abstract and conclusion, substantially expanding v1’s benchmark-and-prompting contribution.

C2.justification: v3 develops distinct shortcut and illusion interpretations of control/manipulation outcomes and offers a mechanism for concept-description prompting benefits. Section 6 newly considers whether human-level intelligence requires human core knowledge, discussing multiple realizability, grounded cognition, and world models. This substantially extends v1’s interpretation of reversed performance and counting failures as evidence against genuine understanding.

D1.justification: Appendices B–D substantially expand documentation of task construction, media handling, matching procedures, Llama3.1-70B/DeepSeek judging, and inference on eight A100 80GB GPUs with size-dependent allocation. These are newly documented details, not proof that all underlying procedures changed. Conversely, v1’s resizing specification and human recruitment/skip instructions are omitted.

R1.justification: v3 replaces the brief architecture-focused overview with benchmark-focused related work and substantially expands positioning around innate knowledge, grounded cognition, world models, and scaling. Added references include Moravec, Barsalou, Lake and colleagues, and Kaplan and colleagues. Much Piaget/Spelke background is retained, while the contribution is repositioned around diagnosing core knowledge deficits.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The narrative is reorganized into benchmark construction, experiments, Concept Hacking, and discussion. Much existing cognitive background moves to Appendix A, technical material is reorganized and expanded in Appendices B–D, and prompting moves to Appendix F. These are substantial structural changes beyond the added scientific content.

P2.justification: The main text switches from one to two columns. The cognitive map and example panels are redesigned, while v1’s accuracy bar chart and model heatmap give way to normalized distributions and a selected-model table. New correlation, scaling, manipulation, and matching displays are added. Prompt results become boxplots, and the original interleaved-media example moves to Appendix B.

improvement.justification: v1’s broad claims about understanding relied mainly on accuracy patterns and one counting example. v3 substantially strengthens their empirical basis through paired interventions, quantitative dependency/scaling analyses, and much fuller curation and evaluation documentation. These changes make the hypotheses more testable and the procedures more auditable. The gains outweigh remaining weaknesses, including inconsistent dataset totals, the contradictory failure-rate equation, undefined uncertainty displays, and scaling conclusions stronger than the reported comparisons establish.
